recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future modernization of the RFC link or broader server-specific lastUpdated guidance should be handled under a new HTTP editorial issue or the separate lastUpdated issue family, not as missing FHIR-20211 application.
issue_request: FHIR-20211 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core HTTP change request asking for a note that HTTP Last-Modified derives from meta.lastUpdated but uses a different format than the FHIR instant value.
initial_application: Commit 0a1dbe19f6 added the requested note to source/http.html, and commit 7b129e2288 corrected XHTML syntax around it. The note remains in the current source.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml lists http.html as the RESTful API page under Exchange, confirming build scope. Later Meta.lastUpdated context, including FHIR-45047 and implementer discussion, clarifies that Last-Modified and meta.lastUpdated can be equivalent instants despite different string formats; it does not conflict with the existing note. No Confluence reference to FHIR-20211 was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because source/http.html:215 already says the Last-Modified header should come from .meta.lastUpdated, that .meta.lastUpdated is a FHIR instant, and that Last-Modified has a different format with MDN and RFC 7232 links.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied Meta.lastUpdated clarification keeps equivalence to HTTP Last-Modified while describing server-specific behavior; already represented on the combined branch and not independently decided here.
Later Applied HTTP Date header issue removed unrelated Date-header timezone wording from the same HTTP page and does not alter the Last-Modified note.

Earlier Published issue about Meta.lastUpdated and Bundle.response.lastModified semantic equivalence provides background but concerns batch/transaction response metadata rather than HTTP header formatting.

Later Resolved-change-required document-date issue treats lastUpdated as server-specific; it is outside the default applied/published source-edit scope and does not require changing the HTTP header note.
